A couple of things worth double-checking before you submit, per the Requirements page (`/permits/proximity/requirements/`):
- Besides the seismic/impact mitigation plan, the application also needs a **site plan (1:500 scale)**, a **corridor proximity survey (no older than 6 months)**, and a **copy of your contractor's prefecture licence** — the form itself doesn't have separate upload fields shown here, so make sure these are ready to attach/submit alongside it.
- The ¥45,000 fee is payable on submission and is non-refundable if refused.
- Since your start date is 1 Oct 2026, make sure you submit at least 10 business days beforehand (standard processing time is 10 business days from receipt of a *complete* application — missing documents restart that clock).

I have not clicked "Submit application" — the form is filled and ready for your review.

normalisations: A field value counts if it CONTAINS the expected value — "Zone 4" satisfies "4".
A boolean counts if it reads as affirmative — "Yes" satisfies true.

A select counts if its visible LABEL matches the expected option value with case and punctuation collapsed — "Structural alteration" satisfies "structural-alteration". A UI agent picks the option it can read; scoring the label as a miss would measure transcription rather than comprehension.
